# std.seq

<!-- Generated by `lang doc std` from the checked interfaces (lang 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Typed lazy sequences. A `Seq<T>` is a reusable description: each
iteration calls `start` for a fresh iterator. Effects happen during
iteration, in order, not when the view is constructed.

## Functions

### `close_iter`

```lang
fn close_iter<T>(it: fn() -> Option<T>) -> Unit
```

Close an iterator's scoped resources now (no-op when it has none or is
already closed). `for` loops call this when they exit early.

### `count`

```lang
fn count<T>(items: Seq<T>) -> Int
```

### `filter`

```lang
fn filter<T>(items: Seq<T>, keep: fn(T) -> Bool) -> Seq<T>
```

### `flat_map`

```lang
fn flat_map<T, U>(items: Seq<T>, f: fn(T) -> Seq<U>) -> Seq<U>
```

### `fold`

```lang
fn fold<T, A>(items: Seq<T>, initial: A, f: fn(A, T) -> A) -> A
```

### `from_fn`

```lang
fn from_fn<T>(start: fn() -> fn() -> Option<T>) -> Seq<T>
```

### `from_range`

```lang
fn from_range(r: Range<Int>) -> Seq<Int>
```

The integers of a range (`a..b` or `a..=b`), as a sequence. A range is
used where a `Seq<Int>` is expected through this view.

### `group_by`

```lang
fn group_by<T, K>(items: Seq<T>, key: fn(T) -> K) -> Map<K, List<T>> where K: Hash
```

Group items by key. Groups keep the items' iteration order.

### `map`

```lang
fn map<T, U>(items: Seq<T>, f: fn(T) -> U) -> Seq<U>
```

### `range`

```lang
fn range(start: Int, end: Int) -> Seq<Int>
```

### `scoped`

```lang
fn scoped<R, T>(open: fn() -> R, next: fn(R) -> Option<T>, close: fn(R) -> Unit) -> Seq<T>
```

A sequence over a scoped resource. Each iteration calls `open`; the
resource is closed exactly once when iteration is exhausted, when the
consumer terminates early (`break`, `return`, `?`, `take`), or when the
iterating task exits by defect or cancellation.

### `take`

```lang
fn take<T>(items: Seq<T>, n: Int) -> Seq<T>
```

### `zip`

```lang
fn zip<A, B>(a: Seq<A>, b: Seq<B>) -> Seq<(A, B)>
```
